title: Lentils, spinach and red pepper
why: Lentils and spinach carry iron from plants, which the body absorbs less easily than iron from meat. Vitamin C in the same meal, here from red pepper, helps you absorb more of it.

title: Oats, milk, chia seeds and strawberries
why: Oats bring fiber and manganese, milk adds calcium and B12, chia seeds add plant omega-3, and strawberries cover vitamin C.

title: Salmon, sweet potato and broccoli
why: Salmon is one of the few foods naturally rich in vitamin D, and it adds omega-3 and B12. Sweet potato covers vitamin A, and broccoli vitamins C and K.

title: Black beans, brown rice, avocado and tomato
why: Beans and rice together supply all the protein building blocks you need. Beans are also rich in folate and fiber.

title: Calcium-set tofu, bok choy and sesame seeds
why: A serving of calcium-set tofu gives about as much calcium as a cup of milk, which makes this a strong dairy-free choice.

title: Eggs, UV-exposed mushrooms and spinach
why: Eggs are the easiest everyday source of choline and biotin. UV-exposed mushrooms are one of the very few plant foods rich in vitamin D.

title: Greek yogurt, walnuts and blueberries
why: Covers calcium, B12, iodine and plant omega-3 in one small bowl.

title: Pumpkin seeds, sunflower seeds, Brazil nuts and banana
why: Pumpkin seeds are among the best plant sources of zinc and magnesium. Brazil nuts are so rich in selenium that one or two a day is enough.

title: Sardines, kale and quinoa
why: Canned sardines with their bones give calcium as well as vitamin D, B12 and omega-3. Kale adds vitamins A, C and K.

title: Chickpeas, carrot, red cabbage and pumpkin seeds
why: A plant-only plate that covers folate, fiber, vitamin A, vitamin C, zinc and magnesium.
